audit.accesslog_not_readable.description: cn=accesslog (openldap.accesslog_base) is not readable by the agent's service DN, or does not exist: no Audit source.

audit.acl_log_only.description: Only ACL LOG is readable: failed authentications and denied commands are seen, reads are not (audit level None).

audit.audit_changes_not_audited.description: No enabled server audit specification records audit changes (AUDIT_CHANGE_GROUP): the audit could be stopped, filtered and restarted without a record, so the audit level is at most Limited.

audit.audit_log_filter_not_read.description: The audit_log_filter component is active, but its log file is not configured in agent.yaml (mysql.audit_log), so the agent does not read it.

audit.audit_log_plugin_not_read.description: The audit_log plugin is active, but its log file is not configured in agent.yaml (mysql.audit_log), so the agent does not read it.

audit.auditlog_on_community.description: The auditLog configured in agent.yaml (mongodb.audit_log, format audit_log) needs MongoDB Enterprise or Percona Server for MongoDB, but the server is MongoDB Community: it is not used.

audit.auth_failures_not_seen.description: No failed authentication (AUTHENTICATION_FAILED) read from the CAS audit log in the last 7 days: check that the CAS audit configuration does not exclude it. The level stays Partial.

audit.auth_records_not_seen.description: Limited: CAS audit records were read in the last 24 h, but no successful authentication (AUTHENTICATION_SUCCESS): authentication actions may be excluded from the CAS audit trail.

audit.authcheck_success_pending.description: Partial once the Audit stream has read a successful authCheck record of the auditLog (auditAuthorizationSuccess enabled; none in the last 24 h): reported Limited until then.

audit.digest_consumer_disabled.description: The performance_schema statements_digest consumer is disabled: no statement has a digest, so a performance_schema poll reads every statement's full text (SQL_TEXT, with its literals): the agent's own, when performance_schema is the Audit source, and a replay of it with the agent's credential, address and program name, which is left out like the agent's. Enable the consumer.

audit.failed_logins_not_audited.description: The audit source records no failed logins (SQL Server Audit: no enabled audit specification with FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP; Extended Events: no error_reported event in the session; Firebird trace: log_connections off): failed authentications are not seen.

audit.failed_operations_not_logged.description: {count} naming context(s) where no failed operation is proven to be logged in cn=accesslog in the last 24 h: the agent's read of a missing entry left no record (olcAccessLogSuccess: TRUE logs successful operations only), or it could not be checked yet. Capped or failed exports may go unseen; the level is at most Partial.

audit.full_pending_first_record.description: Full once the Audit stream has read a pgaudit record (none in the last 24 h): reported Partial until then.

audit.general_log_enabled.description: The general query log is enabled; it is not used as an audit source.

audit.history_long_consumer_disabled.description: The performance_schema events_statements_history_long consumer is disabled.

audit.history_not_readable.description: The performance_schema statement history is not readable by the agent's account.

audit.limited_pending_first_record.description: Limited once the Audit stream has read a record of its source (MongoDB server log or profiler, CAS audit log, Redis / Valkey slow log or command log; none in the last 24 h): reported None until then.

audit.log_format_unsupported.description: The CAS audit log holds records but none in the JSON audit format (cas.audit.engine.audit-format: JSON, one record per line): the DEFAULT format is not read, so there is no Audit source.

audit.log_not_readable.description: The audit log configured for the target is not readable by the agent: the file configured in agent.yaml (on CAS and Firebird, also when it is refused because the agent could write it or one of its parent directories), or on Redis / Valkey none of SLOWLOG, COMMANDLOG and ACL LOG.

audit.log_plugin_mismatch.description: The audit log configured in agent.yaml has no matching active audit plugin logging statements in a supported format: it is not used.

audit.log_readable_by_others.description: A uid other than root, the server's account and the agent's account can read the Firebird trace log, a rotated file it still tracks or new files in its directory (mode bits, groups, access or default ACLs; also when a group's members cannot be enumerated, or the agent's identity files are not the host's): that account sees the logged statements, passwords set through SQL included, and every live token. Partial is withheld while it lasts.

audit.log_records_ambiguous.description: {count} Firebird trace record(s) in the last 24 h could not be told apart from text a client wrote (a forged or split record, an unexpected header token, a cut text, a database path matched only by file name or inode, an unconfirmed server run): each is reported as a read of * by an unchecked principal, and the level is Limited for 24 h. Label run_confirmation_stalled: the stream stopped more than 60 s within one hour waiting for server run confirmations.

audit.log_without_row_counts.description: The audit log carries no row counts: result volumes are unknown.

audit.partial_pending_first_record.description: Partial once the Audit stream has read a record of the audit log (none in the last 24 h): reported Limited until then.

audit.performance_schema_not_readable.description: performance_schema is not readable by the agent's account (no Audit grant).

audit.pgaudit_log_not_configured.description: pgaudit is present; Full needs its log file in agent.yaml (postgres.audit_log).

audit.pgaudit_not_loaded.description: pgaudit settings are set, but the pgaudit library is not loaded (shared_preload_libraries): pgaudit writes no record.

audit.pgaudit_read_class_missing.description: pgaudit.log does not include the read class.

audit.reads_not_logged.description: {count} database(s) or naming context(s) whose reads the audit source does not log. OpenLDAP: no search record in cn=accesslog in the last 24 h, even after a probe search by the agent (olcAccessLogOps without reads, no accesslog overlay on that database, or an olcAccessLogBase that excludes it). SQL Server: no enabled audit specification records reads there (SCHEMA_OBJECT_ACCESS_GROUP, or SELECT on the database).

audit.records_dropped.description: {count} audit log record(s) dropped in the last 24 h: not parsable, oversized or damaged, or (SQL Server, Redis / Valkey, Firebird) lost before the agent read them: rotated or overwritten, or the audit source restarted.

audit.records_dropped_severity.description: {count} pgaudit record(s) dropped in the last 24 h: their severity differs from pgaudit.log_level.

audit.server_audit_filtered.description: The server audit has a WHERE predicate, which can exclude principals or objects: the audit level is at most Limited.

audit.server_audit_not_read.description: server_audit is active ({labels}: logging_on / logging_off, file_output / non_file_output), but its log file is not configured in agent.yaml (mysql.audit_log), so the agent does not read it.

audit.service_ticket_records_not_seen.description: Limited: successful authentications were read from the CAS audit log in the last 24 h, but no service ticket or token issuance record: which application received a ticket is not known.

audit.services_not_audited.description: The Firebird trace services section is not enabled with log_services: backups and user management through the services API are not recorded as services ({labels}).

audit.slow_operations_only.description: The audit source only records the operations the server logs or profiles (MongoDB: slower than slowms, or sampled; Redis / Valkey: the slow log and the command log): fast reads, such as a quick dump of a small collection or keyspace, can go unseen.

audit.source_not_configured.description: No usable Audit source is configured for the target. MongoDB: declare the auditLog or the server log file in agent.yaml (mongodb.audit_log), or grant find on system.profile of the monitored databases. SQL Server: no running Extended Events session with an event_file target, nor an enabled server audit with a FILE target, is named in agent.yaml (sqlserver.audit). Firebird: no firebird.audit block in agent.yaml, or the target is reached through a tunnel (no local log).

audit.sqlserver_audit_needs_control_serv.description: An enabled SQL Server Audit is not an Audit source on SQL Server 2019: reading it through sys.fn_get_audit_file needs CONTROL SERVER, which the agent's account must never hold. An Extended Events session is used instead when one is configured.

audit.statement_consumers_disabled.description: The performance_schema consumers the statement history depends on (global_instrumentation, thread_instrumentation, events_statements_current) are disabled.

audit.statement_text_limit_low.description: The audit source cuts statement texts at {count} bytes (server_audit_query_log_limit, performance_schema_max_sql_text_length, or Firebird's max_sql_length), below the agent's longest statement: the agent's own statements, such as its CAS store guard queries, are cut and reported as reads of * by its account (loud, never quiet). Keep the limit at 1024 or more (Firebird: 4096 or more).

audit.stream_not_available.description: No Audit stream runs for the target: the connector has none in this agent build, or (Redis / Valkey) Audit is not configured or is refused because of the account's privileges. The audit level is reported None, whatever the server logs or profiles.

audit.stream_stopped.description: The Audit stream stopped after {count} internal errors of the agent in a row (the agent log names the code location): the audit level is reported None until Audit is reconfigured or the agent restarts.

audit.trace_config_not_evaluated.description: Limited: the Firebird trace configuration of a declared database could not be evaluated. Labels give the reason: firebird_conf_unreadable, trace_config_unreadable (refused or not parsed), trace_config_file_mismatch, config_changed_since_start, server_process_not_visible, similar_to_pattern (a SIMILAR TO pattern, or _ or % in a file name), databases_conf (alias map not evaluated or changed), foreign_databases_logged (undeclared databases can reach the log), database_path_not_unique (several hard links).

audit.trace_settings_missing.description: Limited: the Firebird trace configuration section of a declared database lacks settings the Partial level needs (enabled, log_filename the declared log, log_connections, log_statement_finish, log_blr_requests, the procedure, function and trigger finish events, log_errors, time_threshold 0, print_perf, no include_filter or exclude_filter, connection_id 0): {labels}.

audit.xe_causality_off.description: The Extended Events session runs without TRACK_CAUSALITY: statements are grouped with their request by session and event order instead (no effect on the audit level).

audit.xe_events_missing.description: The Extended Events session lacks events or actions the agent needs: {count}. The audit level is at most Limited.

audit.xe_session_filtered.description: The Extended Events session filters the events the agent reads, so some statements are not recorded: the audit level is at most Limited.

check.server_is_mariadb.description: The server is MariaDB while the target is declared as mysql.

check.server_is_mysql.description: The server is MySQL while the target is declared as mariadb.

check.server_is_redis.description: The server is Redis while the target is declared as valkey.

check.server_is_valkey.description: The server is Valkey while the target is declared as redis.

check.stage_failed.description: check() failed at stage {labels} (a stage_* label); the cause is last_error.

check.timed_out.description: check() did not finish within its time bound.

coverage.cas_guard_tripped.description: {count} column(s) or field(s) held CAS ticket-id-shaped values: those values were dropped before classification and the columns or fields were not read further (CAS store guard).

coverage.cluster_node_only.description: Cluster node: only the keys of this node ({count}) are read; declare each node as a target to cover the whole cluster.

coverage.computed_columns_not_sampled.description: {count} computed column(s) not sampled: reading them can run user code (a function in the column's expression; on SQLite, a VIRTUAL generated column's expression taken from the file).

coverage.encrypted_columns.description: {count} Always Encrypted column(s) not sampled: the server holds their ciphertext only.

coverage.external_file_tables.description: {count} external-file table(s) not sampled: reading them makes the server read a file outside the database (counted in skipped_remote).

coverage.file_path_refused.description: The declared SQLite path or a file next to it is refused: a symbolic link in the path, not a regular file, more than one hard link, the same file as another target, a refused location (the agent's own state, configuration or key files), a -wal, -shm or -journal file of another owner or on another file system, or an open file that is not the checked one.

coverage.filesystem_not_read_only.description: The file system holding the SQLite file is not mounted read-only for the agent: mount its directory read-only (systemd ProtectSystem=strict or BindReadOnlyPaths=, a :ro bind mount in a container). The file is refused until then.

coverage.hot_journal_pending.description: The SQLite database has a hot rollback journal (an interrupted write the application has not recovered yet): it cannot be read without writing, so it is not read until the application recovers it at its next open.

coverage.masked_columns.description: {count} column(s) under dynamic data masking were sampled as the agent's account sees them, masked: finding nothing there does not mean that they hold no sensitive data.

coverage.module_types_not_sampled.description: {count} key pattern(s) of module types (JSON documents, time series, Bloom filters, vector sets…) not sampled.

coverage.network_filesystem_refused.description: The SQLite file is on a network or FUSE file system (NFS, SMB / CIFS, 9P, Ceph, AFS, Coda, Lustre, GPFS, FUSE): file locks and the WAL index are not reliable there, so the file is refused.

coverage.other_engine_tables.description: {count} table(s) with a storage engine outside the local-data allow-list, not sampled.

coverage.reader_process_failed.description: {count} SQLite reader process failure(s) in the last scan (killed by a signal, out of its limits, or broken off on an invalid message): each cost one unit of work; after 3 the scan stopped for this target. The agent process is not affected.

coverage.reader_sandbox_unavailable.description: The sandboxed SQLite reader process cannot run on this host (no Landlock in the kernel, or a sandbox step failed): the agent opens no SQLite file without it.

coverage.registry_files_skipped.description: {count} CAS service registry file(s) skipped: not readable, refused (symbolic or hard link, writable by the agent), too large, not a service definition or not parsable. None of their values is classified.

coverage.relations_rls_skipped.description: {count} relation(s) skipped because of row-level security (ADR-0012).

coverage.relations_without_select.description: {count} relation(s) without SELECT for the agent's role, not sampled.

coverage.remote_engine_tables.description: {count} table(s) whose rows live on another server, never read (I5): a remote-access storage engine on MySQL / MariaDB; external tables or Stretch Database tables on SQL Server.

coverage.rls_not_verifiable.description: {count} database(s) whose row-level security policies are not visible to the agent's account: every table there was skipped, since the agent cannot tell which ones run a security predicate.

coverage.rollback_mode_not_read.description: The SQLite database is in rollback-journal mode, where every read delays the application's commits: it is not read unless sqlite.rollback_mode is read in agent.yaml for this target (counted in skipped_unsupported).

coverage.schemas_without_usage.description: {count} schema(s) without USAGE for the agent's role, not covered.

coverage.timeseries_not_readable.description: {count} time-series collection(s) refused to the agent's account in the last scan (their reads may need find on their bucket collections, system_buckets resource).

coverage.unrecognized_file_format.description: The declared SQLite file is not a database file the agent reads: its header is not a SQLite 3 header within the supported file format range (an encrypted, compressed or other file), the file is not a database, or its schema cannot be loaded (syntax newer than the bundled SQLite, a schema entry above the length limits, corruption). Nothing was sampled.

coverage.views_not_sampled.description: {count} view(s) not sampled (their base tables or collections are).

coverage.virtual_tables_not_sampled.description: {count} virtual table(s) not sampled: reading them would run a module's code. Their shadow tables, which hold the indexed content, are ordinary tables and are sampled.

coverage.wal_files_not_readable.description: The SQLite database is in WAL mode and its -wal and -shm files are missing (no application holds the file open), only one exists, one is unreadable, the -wal is above 128 MiB, or the WAL index cannot be read without writing: the file is not read; it is read again while the application holds it open.

privilege.accesslog_without_audit.description: cn=accesslog is readable while no Audit stream runs for the target: other users' search filters, compared values and old values are readable.

privilege.admin_commands.description: {count} administration command(s) allowed to the account (for example CONFIG SET, MODULE LOAD, DEBUG, ACL SETUSER, REPLICAOF, MIGRATE): with any command of the refusal list, Discovery and Audit do not run for this target.

privilege.any_database.description: A privilege applies to every database (for example readAnyDatabase, or a resource with an empty database name): databases created later are readable too.

privilege.audit_grant_without_audit.description: The account holds an Audit permission ({labels}) while no Audit stream uses it: revoke it, or configure Audit for the target.

privilege.beyond_select.description: {count} privilege(s) beyond SELECT on databases, tables or columns; the most severe: {labels}.

privilege.cluster_actions.description: {count} cluster-wide action(s) (for example inprog, serverStatus, getCmdLineOpts): other sessions' operations and server settings are visible.

privilege.config_readable.description: The engine's configuration is readable by the agent's account. OpenLDAP: cn=config is readable by the agent's service DN (access control rules, root password hashes, every server setting). CAS: CAS configuration files (cas.properties, cas.yml, application.yml or .properties) sit in the declared service registry directory and hold every CAS secret: the registry source is refused and those files are never opened.

privilege.database_file_writable.description: The SQLite file, one of its -wal, -shm or -journal files, or a directory on its path is writable by the agent's account: the agent must only read, so the file is refused until the agent's write access is removed.

privilege.database_roles.description: {count} database role membership(s) other than public (and db_datareader when extended_grants is set); the most severe: {labels}.

privilege.declared_keys_not_readable.description: {count} declared key pattern(s) or database(s) the account cannot read: Discovery skips them (check redis.key_patterns and redis.databases in agent.yaml against the account's ACL).

privilege.extended_variant.description: Extended-variant grants, expected because extended_grants is set: {labels}.

privilege.global_privileges.description: {count} global or server-level privilege(s) beyond those the agent needs (MySQL / MariaDB: other than SELECT and USAGE; SQL Server: server permissions other than CONNECT SQL and VIEW ANY DATABASE; Firebird: system privileges, a credential relation other than the account's own SEC$USERS row readable, or the server configuration readable through RDB$CONFIG); the most severe: {labels}.

privilege.global_select.description: Global SELECT: system tables are readable, including mysql.user password hashes.

privilege.grant_option.description: A privilege of the account is WITH GRANT OPTION.

privilege.not_evaluated.description: Privileges not evaluated: the account name could not be matched, or a privilege list could not be fully read (cut at its limit, rows skipped, or its query failed): on MongoDB, connectionStatus not readable; on PostgreSQL, the CAS store guard's candidate relation or column list (also a name not UTF-8); on SQL Server, a check read such as logon triggers (hidden from the minimal grants, never reported absent); on Redis 6.2, the ACL (no ACL DRYRUN); on Firebird, the role graph. Reads: {labels}.

privilege.password_attributes_readable.description: The agent's service DN can read userPassword or authPassword values (seen with an attributes-only search: the values were not read).

privilege.performance_schema_unused.description: SELECT on performance_schema is unused (the audit log is the Audit source): the statement text of every session is readable, with clear-text passwords on MariaDB.

privilege.performance_schema_without_aud.description: SELECT on performance_schema while no Audit stream runs for the target: the statement text of every session is readable.

privilege.predefined_roles.description: Member of predefined roles beyond the minimal grants: {labels}.

privilege.pubsub_channels.description: {count} pub/sub command(s) allowed to the account (PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE): set resetchannels.

privilege.read_beyond_discovery.description: {count} read action(s) or command(s) beyond those Discovery uses (MongoDB: beyond find and listCollections, for example changeStream, which streams every future write, dbHash or listIndexes; Redis / Valkey: for example GET, HGETALL, KEYS or DUMP).

privilege.refused.description: The agent's account holds a right it must never hold ({labels}): Discovery and Audit do not run for this target until it is revoked.

privilege.registry_writable.description: {count} CAS service registry file(s) or directories writable by the agent's account (directly, through its groups or an ACL, or through a parent directory), so the registry is not read from them: the agent must only read service definitions, since an account that can write them could change what CAS releases to whom.

privilege.role_attributes.description: Role attributes beyond the minimal grants: {labels}.

privilege.roles_not_evaluated.description: {count} granted role(s) whose privileges are not evaluated.

privilege.scripting.description: {count} scripting command(s) allowed to the account (EVAL, EVALSHA, FCALL, FUNCTION LOAD…): server-side code execution, so Discovery and Audit do not run for this target.

privilege.server_roles.description: {count} server role membership(s) other than public; the most severe: {labels}.

privilege.system_collections.description: Access to system collections or to the admin, local or config databases: credentials, the oplog, other users' profiled queries or stored JavaScript may be readable.

privilege.system_database_select.description: SELECT on the mysql or sys system database.

privilege.ticket_credentials_readable.description: The agent's account can read credential columns of a CAS ticket registry or audit trail (ticket ids, bodies, principals, attributes, AUD_RESOURCE, AUD_HEADERS), directly, through a role or PUBLIC, or through a schema- or database-wide grant: grant SELECT on the metadata columns only (Redis / Valkey: guarded keys, so declare positive key patterns). The agent never reads them.

privilege.write_actions.description: {count} write or administration action(s) (for example insert, update, remove, drop, index, user or role management).

privilege.write_not_evaluated.description: Write access of the service DN is not evaluated: OpenLDAP shows a read-only account neither its access control rules nor its effective rights. Check olcAccess (docs/05-security.md).

security.audit_headers_logged.description: CAS audit records carry request headers (cas.audit.engine.http-request-headers), so the audit log holds cookies, including the ticket-granting cookie: remove headers from the audited fields. The agent skips them.

security.client_secrets_in_clear.description: {count} CAS service definition(s) with an OAuth or OIDC client secret in clear: encrypt them. The agent never samples, masks nor fingerprints a client secret.

security.default_user_nopass.description: The server's default user is enabled without a password: anyone who reaches the server has its rights ({count} command(s) of the agent's refusal list allowed to it).

security.file_world_readable.description: The SQLite database file is readable by every local user: every account of the host can read its data. Restrict it to the application and the agent's group.

security.firebird_tunnel.description: The Firebird target is reached through a tunnel the operator runs (firebird.tunnel in agent.yaml): its security is the operator's, and the target has no Audit.

security.init_connect.description: init_connect is set: SQL runs at every login of the agent's account.

security.login_event_trigger.description: An enabled login event trigger runs user code at every connection of the agent (Firebird: an ON CONNECT database trigger; ON TRANSACTION START triggers too, in the agent's log).

security.ticket_registry_unencrypted.description: {count} CAS ticket(s) stored without ticket registry encryption (crypto.enabled false): ticket ids and principals are in clear in the table or collection. The agent read only the ticket types and counts.

security.tls_disabled.description: TLS disabled on a network connection (tls: disable_insecure): traffic in clear, read-only not guaranteed.
